chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Mut'ah, by Allah, is superior, and with it the Quran was revealed, and the Sunnah proceeded.
ai.seo_question: What is the status of Al-Mut'ah in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts the superiority of Al-Mut'ah, linking its validity directly to Quranic revelation and established Prophetic Sunnah. This statement is central to the Shia jurisprudential debate regarding whether the prohibition of Mut'ah marriage was abrogated or permanent, with Shia scholars citing this narration as evidence for its enduring permissibility. The reference to the Quran descending in conjunction with it underscores its divine origin and legitimacy within the early Muslim community.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Tamatto , by Allahazwj, is superior, and Quran Revealed with it, and the Sunnah flowed by it’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Hajj. He (the Imam) said, ‘Make it al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous).’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘When we will stand before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, we will say, “O our Lord, we followed Your book and the Sunnah of Your Holy prophet, but people will say, ‘We looked into our minds (opinions) and we followed them.”””
